text:
jamal: heads up — noticed a recurring isolation pattern across 3 dedicated customers over the last 2 weeks. all started after small config changes to onprem peers.
maria: can you dump the timeline and affected peers?
jamal: quick list: cust-A (INC-4521) 03/12, cust-B (INC-4578) 03/15, cust-C (INC-4602) 03/18. symptoms: KV cache stalls + partial vpc peering flaps.
kai: is this the same root cause as last quarter, or a new regression?
jamal: similar surface-level networking flaps but different trigger — this time an edge NAT timeout + onprem firewall reordering.
sophia: omg reordering again. we patched a mitigation but not the runbook.
sre-bot: deploy noticed: canary after 03/11 config push flagged increased TCP retransmits on dedicated nodes (alert id: net-3344).
maria: action items proposal: 1) short-term: add per-customer prefix-safe retry and prefix cache TTL tweak (owner: kai, ETA: 48h). 2) mid-term: update runbook with onprem peering checklist + test harness (owner: sophia, ETA: 1w). 3) long-term: add automated regression detector for vpc-peering patterns (owner: jamal, ETA: 3w).
kai: ack. I'll open an infra task and attach a smoke script. ticket: INF-2890.
jamal: adding notes to postmortem doc and tagging customers for remediation window. will propose maintenance windows in the doc.
sophia: for the runbook update, can we include a small test snippet to verify TCP window reordering? sample: ```bash
# run from onprem test host
for i in {1..50}; do curl -H 'X-Test: peering' https://edge.example.internal/health || echo fail; sleep 1; done
```
maria: good. also add a checklist item: verify HSM/KMS access isn't being throttled during bursts — we saw a correlation for cust-B.
jamal: ownerships: kai => infra fixes + INF-2890, sophia => runbook + RB-102, jamal => pattern detector + PD-77. I'll set up weekly checkpoints until PD-77 lands.
sophia: i'll draft the runbook PR by EOD tomorrow and include explicit rollback steps and a minimal canary config.
kai: INF-2890 will include a canary job and a rollback automation step. ETA 48h, will ping here when ready.
maria: customers contacted for weekend windows? two said prefer late-night maintenance. I'll coordinate scheduling.
jamal: blockers: need a list of all onprem firewall vendors we saw; sophia can you prod support for that table?
sophia: on it, sharing table by EOD: Palo Alto, Fortinet, Cisco ASA, and an internal appliance for cust-C.
sre-bot: reminder: postmortem follow-up sync scheduled in #incidents in 24h.
maria: quick risk note — isolation bugs tend to recur in cohorts after config pushes. we should treat "cohort regression" as a standard mode in the postmortem template.
jamal: agreed. adding a new section: "Cohort regression signal checklist" with examples, thresholds, and quick mitigations.
kai: will also add a telemetry flag in the serving runtime so we can tag requests by peering-session id for easier triage.
sophia: PR link when ready: https://git.redwood.local/r/runbooks/peering-playbook/pull/12 (draft).
maria: thanks. can we have a short postmortem follow-up report by Friday with owners, tickets, and customer windows?
jamal: yes — i'll compile and ping legal for any customer comms review.
sophia: marking items as: INF-2890 (in-progress), RB-102 (draft), PD-77 (planning).
jamal: closing note: let's treat this as a template for future dedicated/private cohort regressions. small, frequent checks will help avoid broad customer impact. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks everyone. next check-in in 24h.
